newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish grain loss from floods seen up to 800,000 T.
newsitem.headline: Polish grain loss from floods seen up to 800,000 T.

text.p: Poland's grain harvest will be cut by 600,000 to 800,000 tonnes as a result of floods in southern Poland, according to preliminary estimates given by the agriculture minister on Tuesday.
Jaroslaw Kalinowski told reporters during a break in a cabinet meeting no firm estimates had been made of flood damage, but it was assumed that at least 165-180,000 hectares of grain were flooded.

"Estimates assume that 400,000 hectares have been flooded. We estimate that out of that about 165,000 to 180,000 were grain," he said, adding that average yield figures suggested the loss amounted to 600,000 to 800,000 tonnes of grain.
Last week Kalinowski said this year's grain harvest was likely to be average at around 23.5-24 million tonnes, with the grain not of very high quality.
Kalinowski said reserves held by the state's Agriculture Market Agency (ARR) and grain wholesalers were sufficient to meet demand and that there was no risk of grain shortages.
He also said the ministry expected good crops in other areas of the country unaffected by the flooding.
"These are substantial losses but they won't worsen the country's grain balance and we should not expect any substantial rise in grain and food prices," he said.
Kalinowksi said the government had agreed to help farmers in the afflicted areas by supplying them with wheat from ARR reserves.
He said farmers would receive free of charge one tonne of wheat for every one hectare of land hit by floods.
Kalinowski said the ministry did not yet have exact figures on how much wheat would be needed although rough estimates were around 250,000 to 300,000 tonnes.
